big: An option's price rises ₹0.60 when the share rises ₹1. It loses ₹2 every day even when nothing moves. It jumps when markets get nervous. Each of these has a Greek name.

lines: They are letters used to name sensitivities. Delta is price change per ₹1 move. Theta is daily time decay. Vega is the effect of volatility. Implied volatility is what the market expects, read from option prices.

intro: Made-up figures, for learning only. This is education, not a call to trade.
rows: price +₹0.60 per ₹1 rise in the share
loses about ₹2 a day with no move
price shifts when volatility shifts 1 point
note: Theta works against the buyer and for the seller.

title: The Greeks
stops: Delta shows price change for a ₹1 move in the underlying
Higher implied volatility makes options costlier
caps: It also hints at finishing in the money.
